article_title: Formative Research in Ubiquitous and Virtual Environments in Higher Education
citation: Cristian Velandia-Mesa, Francisca-José Serrano-Pastor, María-José Martínez-Segura. (2017). Formative Research in Ubiquitous and Virtual Environments in Higher Education. Comunicar, 51, XXV. https://doi.org/10.3916/C51-2017-01
title: 41-item four-level evaluation rubric for research competence
description: The evaluation instrument used to measure research competence in both groups, built from evaluation rubrics referencing models of research in ubiquitous and mobile contexts in higher education. "The instrument has 41 items, each with four levels of achievement": ten items value referencing-stage outcomes, twenty value systematization strategies, and eleven value analysis and reflection. Reliability analyses showed high internal consistency with "a value of α≥ 0.80".
requirements: Cronbach's Alpha model and Guttman's split-half reliability method were used to verify internal consistency
target_learning_goals: Assessment of formative research competence across referencing, systematization, and analysis
examples: Applied at pretest and at the three intervention points to generate the mean scores compared between groups.

citation: de Andres Crespo M, Lykoudis P, Myint F, Berlingieri P. (2025). Surgery and technical skill decay. International Journal of Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1097/JS9.0000000000002313
title: 41-study evidence base on surgical technical skill decay (Table 1)
description: A curated corpus of 41 peer-reviewed original studies on skill decay in surgery, identified via a four-database search of ("skills decay" OR "skills fade") AND "surgery" on 18 August 2024, yielding 162 articles before screening. Table 1 tabulates each study's participants, assessment methods, procedures tested and findings, spanning laparoscopic, robotic, arthroscopic, cricothyroidotomy and microsurgical skills with retention intervals from 1 month to 2 years. The review reports "The majority of studies included (83%, 34/41) had fewer than 50 participants."
requirements: Studies had to be peer-reviewed, published original research specific to surgical skill decay with quantitative measurement data
constraints: Heterogeneous study designs and outcome measures meant no meta-analyses could be performed
83% of included studies (34/41) had fewer than 50 participants
target_learners: surgical trainees and educators designing retention or return-to-work training
target_learning_goals: understanding which surgical skills decay and how to mitigate decay
examples: Included studies range from De Win's 145 medical students across six spacing schedules to Howells' six consultant orthopedic surgeons tested on arthroscopic Bankart sutures
key_sources: de Andres Crespo M, Lykoudis P, Myint F, Berlingieri P. (2025). Surgery and technical skill decay. International Journal of Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1097/JS9.0000000000002313
